Near Mint condition cards appear 'fresh out of the pack,' with edges and surfaces virtually free from all flaws. ' ' ' ' Lightly Played (LP)' Lightly Played condition cards can have slight border or corner wear, or possibly minor scratches. No major defects are present, and there are less than 4 total flaws on the card. Lightly Played condition foils may have slight fading or indications of wear on the card face. ' ' ' ' Moderately Played (MP)' Moderately Played condition cards have moderate wear, or flaws apparent to the naked eye. Moderately Played condition cards can show moderate border wear, mild corner wear, water damage, scratches , creases or fading, light dirt buildup, or any combination of these defects. ' ' ' ' Heavily Played (HP)' Heavily Played condition cards exhibit signs of heavy wear. Heavily Played condition cards may include cards that have significant creasing, folding, severe water damage, heavy whitening, heavy border wear, and /or tearing. ' ' ' ' Damaged (D)' Damaged condition cards show obvious tears, bends, or creases that could make the card illegal for tournament play, even when sleeved. Damaged condition cards have massive border wear, possible writing or major inking (ex. white-bordered cards with black-markered front borders), massive corner wear, prevalent scratching, folds, creases or tears. I've been enjoying Azul queens garden! I haven't played the other installments (yet!), but I do really enjoy how puzzly it feels. There isn't THAT much player interaction, but picking tiles from a common pool does add a layer of strategy that I apreciate. Trying to get the tiles you want before your opponent, trying to avoid refreshing the stack or flipping a hexagon over so your opponent has less selection, I've even taken some less than desirable tiles that my opponent wanted. The tiles placement/discarding is where the game really shines though! I really enjoy the feel of creating patterns and managing my storage to get as many points as possible. There are JUST enough colors and patterns to make it difficult to get a set, but not so many as to make set collecting impossible. So far the game definitely plays more aroung the 60mins+ mark than the 45mins. All around a realy good thinky puzzly game with great production value! R Planet Unknown: Supermoon Ron Lindeen Space Tetris An easy to explain, easy to play game. I have not played enough to use the more complex components, but I don't believe it's going to get complex. One caveat, the base game does not come with a cover for the lazy susan. It comes with the expansion. I don't know what they were thinking. Near Mint condition cards appear 'fresh out of the pack,' with edges and surfaces virtually free from all flaws. ' ' ' ' Lightly Played (LP)' Lightly Played condition cards can have slight border or corner wear, or possibly minor scratches. No major defects are present, and there are less than 4 total flaws on the card. Lightly Played condition foils may have slight fading or indications of wear on the card face. ' ' ' ' Moderately Played (MP)' Moderately Played condition cards have moderate wear, or flaws apparent to the naked eye. Moderately Played condition cards can show moderate border wear, mild corner wear, water damage, scratches , creases or fading, light dirt buildup, or any combination of these defects. ' ' ' ' Heavily Played (HP)' Heavily Played condition cards exhibit signs of heavy wear. Heavily Played condition cards may include cards that have significant creasing, folding, severe water damage, heavy whitening, heavy border wear, and /or tearing. ' ' ' ' Damaged (D)' Damaged condition cards show obvious tears, bends, or creases that could make the card illegal for tournament play, even when sleeved. Damaged condition cards have massive border wear, possible writing or major inking (ex. white-bordered cards with black-markered front borders), massive corner wear, prevalent scratching, folds, creases or tears.
